title: The Clean Contact
premise: Gideon Nystrom, a traumatized interpreter hiding in a Geneva safe house after a botched extraction left a colleague dead, discovers the house listed online with photos revealing her own belongings — proof that someone inside her protection detail is selling her location. Tasked with extracting Marek Voss, a defector carrying evidence of a peace-process betrayal, she realizes he may be deliberate bait to flush out everyone who knows too much. As Gideon traces the leak through layers of loyalty and forged identities, she learns her own name was invented by the service that now wants her erased. In the end, she trades the defector's evidence for her real identity, burns the network from within, and walks out of Geneva as someone new — finally able to sleep.
about_author: Yara Nakamura is a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass booths in politically fragile negotiations before turning to fiction. She writes spare, claustrophobic thrillers about people whose professions demand they disappear into other people's words.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Scrolling property listings at 3 a.m., she finds the safe house for sale — photos include her coat on the hook, her books on the shelf. Panic masquerading as calm; she reports it and is told to stand down. Emotional beat: the floor of her invisibility gives way.

chapters.title: Booth Nine
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Gideon's POV. The incident: an interpretation session where a mistranslated phrase preceded the ambush that killed her colleague Ilse. Guilt rendered as memory fragments. Emotional beat: establishing what 'the incident' cost her.

chapters.title: Delegation of One
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Her handler, Brandt, assigns her one last job: extract defector Marek Voss during the failing peace summit's final week. She notes his evasiveness about who requested her specifically. Emotional beat: reluctant re-entry into the game.

chapters.title: The Man Who Speaks Five Ways
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Waiting in a transit hotel, Marek rehearses his cover story, aware he's being watched by his own escorts. He suspects the delegation is theater but needs Gideon anyway. Emotional beat: charm stretched over fear.

chapters.title: Contact Protocol
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. First meeting with Marek at a lakeside kiosk; their coded exchange goes slightly wrong when he uses a phrase only Ilse knew. Someone fed him her history. Emotional beat: recognition — this is bait, or a test.

chapters.title: Housekeeping
chapters.summary: Supporting agent Lena Roth's POV. Lena sweeps the safe house, finds a second set of keys and a hidden camera freshly installed. She says nothing to Brandt. Emotional beat: complicity beginning; loyalty bending.

chapters.title: The Summit That Was Always Dying
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, interpreting at the summit. She hears delegates negotiate in bad faith and catches a delegate referencing 'the interpreter problem' — herself. Emotional beat: from witness to target.

chapters.title: Ilse's Grammar
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Digging into Ilse's effects, she finds notes suggesting Ilse had discovered the leak before dying — and that the mistranslation may have been deliberate, by someone else. Emotional beat: guilt cracking into suspicion.

chapters.title: Two Keys
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Confronted obliquely by Gideon, Lena admits the camera but claims she reported it upward — to a man who doesn't exist on any org chart. Emotional beat: alliance of the expendable.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek confesses partially: he was sent as bait to identify which handlers still protect their assets. He believes Gideon is the actual prize. Emotional beat: transactional honesty deepening into trust.

chapters.title: Extraction Window
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Planning the move across the border during the summit's closing gala; Brandt insists on a route Gideon recognizes as the same corridor where Ilse died. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating Gideon and Marek amid the closing reception. A delegate slips Gideon a keycard; Marek is briefly taken aside by men without badges. Emotional beat: the mask of diplomacy slipping in public.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The extraction begins — trains, a freight yard, a forged passport with Gideon's face under a name she's never used. It works too smoothly. Emotional beat: adrenaline curdling into certainty they're being allowed through.

chapters.title: The Corridor
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena follows the same route Ilse died on and finds the surveillance blind spot wasn't a mistake — it was purchased. She calls Gideon with a warning cut short. Emotional beat: sacrifice; the phone going dead.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe
chapters.summary: Gideon and Marek's shared POV. Holed up in a secondary site, they decrypt Ilse's notes: the leak is Brandt, and Gideon's identity was manufactured by the network itself. Emotional beat: the self dissolving — who was she before?

chapters.title: What Brandt Built
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV, first time. His rationale: the peace process needed controlled failures, and interpreters were his instruments. He orders the secondary site hit. Emotional beat: chilling bureaucratic certainty.

chapters.title: The Real Name
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Following Ilse's trail to a records office, Gideon finds her original identity — a person erased at nineteen, with living family. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into purpose.

chapters.title: Turnabout
chapters.summary: Gideon and Marek's POV. Instead of running, they feed Brandt false coordinates through the compromised channel, using his own leak against him. Emotional beat: hunter and hunted exchanging places.

chapters.title: The Clean Contact
chapters.summary: Climax, Gideon's POV. At the rendezvous, Brandt arrives expecting surrender; Gideon has already delivered the evidence to three delegations simultaneously. Confrontation in the empty safe house — the one from the listing. Emotional beat: facing the architect of her erasure.

chapters.title: Loose Threads
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Brandt detained by his own masters; Lena alive, recovering; Marek granted asylum but choosing silence over testimony. Emotional beat: justice partial, survival imperfect.

chapters.title: Interpreting Silence
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She visits her family under her real name, unable to explain the years, choosing not to try. She declines the service's offer of a new alias. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning with identity as chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: First Sleep
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, final chapter. In a rented flat with no history, she unpacks the coat from the listing photo and hangs it on a new hook. She sleeps through the night. Final line echoes the opening listing. Emotional beat: resolution — invisibility traded for authorship of self.
